scams.name: Grand Palace 'Closed' Tuk-Tuk Gem Shop Tour
scams.description: You walk up to the Grand Palace entrance on Thanon Na Phra Lan and a friendly man in a pressed shirt — often introducing himself as a teacher or 'palace officer' — greets you with 'Welcome! Where are you from?' Before you can orient yourself he tells you the palace is 'closed until 1 PM for a royal ceremony' and helpfully flags down a waiting tuk-tuk that will take you on a loop of 'beautiful hidden temples' for just 20 baht. A u/RobotMaster1 r/ThailandTourism thread titled 'I filmed the Grand Palace is closed scam in Bangkok' (226 upvotes, 59 comments) documents the exact choreography: the first stop is a lesser wat, the second is a 'government tailor,' the third is a gem shop where polished staff in suits produce 'investment grade' sapphires with laminated certificates.
scams.avoidance: Verify Grand Palace hours the same day on the official royalgrandpalace.th website or Google Maps before leaving your hotel Enter the Grand Palace through the main Visitor Centre gate on Na Phra Lan — ignore anyone who intercepts you on the walk from the river or Sanam Luang Never accept a tuk-tuk 'tour' priced under 300 baht — at that price the driver's revenue comes entirely from shop commissions Book suits only from vetted tailors with posted prices (e.g., Tailor on Ten or Rajawongse on Sukhumvit Soi 4) — never from a shop you were taken to If you're already in the tour, politely decline to enter any shop; the driver's revenue model collapses at the first refusal and they will drop you
scams.location: Grand Palace, Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Chao Phraya riverfront entrances

scams.name: Suvarnabhumi Airport Taxi Meter Refusal
scams.description: You land at Suvarnabhumi, make it to the official taxi queue in the basement of Terminal 1, and get assigned Car 847. The driver nods, loads your bags, and says '500 baht to Sukhumvit, no meter.' The legitimate metered fare to central Sukhumvit is ฿220–฿350 plus about ฿50 in tolls. At 2 AM and loaded with luggage, 500 baht feels manageable and you accept. You've just lost roughly $5 to a Thailand-oldest scam that r/Bangkok ('No meter taxi,' comments/1bb7e1e) and r/ThailandTourism ('Taxis not using the meter – is this just how it is?', comments/1kcliob) have logged thousands of variants of. The airport queue is governed by rules requiring meter use — but enforcement collapses between 11 PM and 6 AM, exactly when jet-lagged tourists arrive.
scams.avoidance: At Suvarnabhumi, skip the airport taxi queue entirely at peak scam hours (11 PM–6 AM) and take the Airport Rail Link City Line (฿45, 45 min to Phaya Thai) If you take an airport taxi, insist on 'meter, please — Motorway' before getting in; if refused, walk to the next car without negotiation Use Grab or Bolt from anywhere in the city — the app guarantees a fixed price and records the route, which eliminates meter games and padded detours Know the expected fare: BKK → Sukhumvit metered is roughly ฿220–฿350 plus ฿45–฿75 in tolls; DMK → Sukhumvit is ฿300–฿400 If a driver quotes a flat rate, photograph the car's license plate before walking away and report to Tourist Police 1155 — they maintain a complaint database
scams.location: Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK) arrivals level, Don Mueang (DMK), Sukhumvit hotel driveways

scams.name: Patpong / Soi Cowboy Ping Pong Show Drink Bill
scams.description: A tout on Patpong hands you a laminated menu: free entry, '฿100 beers,' and 'free show' upstairs. The show is bizarre but short. When you try to leave, staff block the door and a bill arrives for ฿8,000. The drinks listed on the menu you were shown are not the drinks you were served; the real menu appears now, with small print charging ฿700 per beer and ฿2,000 per 'lady drink' you did not order. r/ThailandTourism 'Horrifying Experience at Patpong Night Market' (comments/1n9bw1d) describes exactly this — three staff standing between the tourist and the exit until the bill is paid in full. Bangkok Post ran a 2023 piece on a French tourist hit with a ฿87,000 bill at a Patpong ping pong venue who eventually paid because bouncers threatened violence.
scams.avoidance: If you want to see a ping pong show, go in the early evening to venues with Google Maps reviews, printed prices at the door, and ideally other tourists already inside Before you sit down, ask in writing: 'Total price for 1 show + 1 beer.' If they won't write a number, walk out Do not accept drinks offered to hostesses, tablemates, or staff — each is billed to you at scam rates Pay each drink at the bar as you order it rather than running a tab — this limits the exposure at billing time If a scam bill arrives and staff block you, calmly call Tourist Police 1155 — venues fold quickly at the word 'police,' and the number is answered 24/7 with English-speaking staff
scams.location: Patpong Soi 1 & 2 (Silom), Soi Cowboy (Sukhumvit Soi 21), Nana Plaza alleys

scams.name: Tuk-Tuk Tailor Suit Scam
scams.description: You come out of Asok BTS and a well-dressed man falls into step: 'My brother has a tailor shop. Sukhumvit 11, very good price. Tuk-tuk takes you for 50 baht, end of the month special.' At the shop a charming tailor measures you up, recommends two suits in 'Super 120 wool' for ฿8,500, and promises delivery in 48 hours. You pay in cash. Two days later the suits arrive: the 'wool' is 40% polyester, the lining is acetate pretending to be silk, and the shoulders slope because the pattern was cut for a different body shape. By the time you notice, your flight is tomorrow. This is the classic Bangkok tailor scam that has been running since at least the 1980s and appears in virtually every 'first-timer in Thailand' thread on r/ThailandTourism, most recently r/ThailandTourism 'I fell for the Suit Tuk Tuk scam' (comments/1i3eal5) and r/Bangkok 'I fell for the TukTuk Suit scam' (comments/1jtaz82).
scams.avoidance: Research tailors before your trip on r/Bangkok and askandyaboutclothes.com; stick to published names (Rajawongse, Narry's, Tailor on Ten, 9 Tailors) that have 10+ year reputations Never follow a tuk-tuk recommendation to any tailor — if the tailor needs a street tout, they're running on commissions not craftsmanship Pay by credit card in stages: a deposit of 20–30% only, with the balance due on satisfactory final fitting Ask to see the actual bolt of fabric and photograph the mill label before fabric is cut; verify the composition matches what you were quoted Build in at least 5 days between first fitting and flight so you have leverage to request corrections; if the tailor can't work in that window, find another shop
scams.location: Sukhumvit (Asok, Nana), Pratunam, around Hua Lamphong train station

scams.name: Fake Monk Donation Racket (Sukhumvit / Asok / Nana)
scams.description: Walking across the Asok BTS skywalk toward Terminal 21, a man in saffron robes steps in front of you holding out a small bronze amulet and a donation book filled with names and amounts — ฿500, ฿2,000, $50. He presses the amulet into your hands, makes a brief blessing gesture, and points at the book. Social pressure takes over; you hand over ฿500 and feel good about it. You shouldn't. r/ThailandTourism 'Monks asking for money sukhumvit/Asoke' (comments/1djxyw9) documents the pattern: 'Chinese fake monks used to be seen only in US and Europe, but now they are shameless enough to scam foreign tourists in Buddhism countries like Thailand.' Real Theravada monks do not solicit cash from tourists on public walkways — genuine alms-giving happens at dawn on the streets near their monastery and involves food, not money.
scams.avoidance: Know that real Thai monks do not solicit cash from tourists on the street — decline with a polite wai and keep walking If you want to make an authentic temple donation, use the official metal donation box inside any wat (Wat Pho, Wat Arun, Wat Benchamabophit all have them) Do not accept any object placed in your hands by a 'monk' — hand it back immediately or drop it and walk on Legitimate morning alms-giving (tak bat) near temples involves food offerings, not cash — never a donation book Report persistent fake monks to Tourist Police 1155 or the Bangkok Metropolitan Police — they keep a database of active offenders
scams.location: Asok and Nana BTS skywalks, Sukhumvit Soi 3–11, Chatuchak Weekend Market

scams.name: Grab / Bolt Cancel-and-Pay-Cash Switch
scams.description: You book a Grab from your hotel to Suvarnabhumi for ฿380. The driver accepts, parks 200 meters away, and sends a chat message in broken English: 'Please cancel booking. Pay me cash ฿800 now.' You have 40 minutes until the airport express leaves. If you cancel, Grab records it as your cancellation (no refund, driver penalty waived, you lose the fare record). If you refuse, the driver idles until the app auto-cancels as a no-show and you get charged a cancellation fee anyway. r/ThailandTourism 'Grab cancellation scam tip' (comments/18z55v1) describes exactly this pattern: drivers send scripted messages claiming motorbike accidents or traffic 'emergencies' to pressure you to cancel and switch to cash at triple the fare.
scams.avoidance: Never cancel a Grab/Bolt booking on the driver's request — respond 'app price only, thank you' and wait for the ride to start If the driver idles for 5+ minutes without moving, cancel yourself from the app (the cancellation logs their behavior, which Grab/Bolt support refunds and penalizes) At Suvarnabhumi, use the designated Grab pickup zone at Level 4 (Departures) — Grab drivers can legally enter this zone Keep screenshots of every booking (fare + route + driver ID) — Grab/Bolt in-app help refunds documented overcharges within 24 hours Default to Grab over Bolt in Bangkok — Grab has tighter driver vetting and faster support response (though neither is immune)
scams.location: Suvarnabhumi (BKK), Don Mueang (DMK), Sukhumvit Soi 11 & 23 pickup points

scams.name: Indian 'Lucky Face' Hair Supplement & Fortune Teller
scams.description: You walk out of Asok BTS and a well-dressed Indian man falls into step, smiles broadly, and says 'You have a very lucky face, sir.' He asks where you're from, makes flattering predictions, then produces a small jar of 'Ayurvedic hair growth paste' or shows you a wallet of 'certified gems' — the pitch pivots depending on your reaction. By the time you realize you haven't said you have hair loss, he's asking for ฿1,500 for a 'lucky blessing' or ฿4,000 for a 'guaranteed' supplement. r/Bangkok 'How does this scam work?' (comments/1mf4wcs) catalogs the standard scripts; r/ThailandTourism 'SCAM ALERT – Can I see your country's currency?' (comments/1pw5o97) describes a parallel currency-view variant where the 'lucky face' compliment is followed by a request to see your local notes, which the scammer then either palms partly or uses to gauge how much cash you're carrying.
scams.avoidance: Do not stop walking when approached — brief eye contact and 'mai ao, khop khun' ('no thanks') works, sustained engagement does not Never hand your wallet, phone, or cash to any stranger for any reason — including 'just to look' or 'to demonstrate' If an item is placed in your hand, drop it on the ground or hand it back once without discussion and walk away Real Ayurvedic practitioners operate out of clinics with addresses — street sellers are all running the same scam Photograph the tout (from a distance) and report to Tourist Police 1155 if they follow or escalate — they track active crews on Sukhumvit
scams.location: Sukhumvit Soi 11, Silom Road, Khao San Road, Asok BTS exits

scams.name: Khao San Road Drink-Spiking & Pickpocket
scams.description: It's 1 AM on Khao San Road and a bar invites you in with buckets of rum-and-Red-Bull for ฿200. You take two, chat with new friends, and wake up in a tuk-tuk with ฿19,500 missing from your wallet, no phone, and no memory of the last four hours. r/Bangkok 'Drugged, robbed and given covid19 in Khao San Bangkok' (comments/xjwx19) describes this incident almost word-for-word: the poster was spiked, removed from the bar, emptied, and tuk-tuk'd back to their hotel. The neighborhood's party atmosphere — Khao San hosts tens of thousands of backpackers nightly — is the perfect cover for the scam, and Bangkok police have flagged the bucket cocktails (small plastic buckets filled with spirits and unknown mixers) as the delivery vehicle of choice.
scams.avoidance: Never accept a bucket cocktail — order bottled beer or cocktails mixed in front of you at the bar Watch your drink being made and keep it in your hand the entire time; discard any drink you set down Travel in groups on Khao San — solo drinking here is the highest-risk scenario Store passport, extra cards, and most cash in your hotel safe; carry only ฿1,000–฿2,000 and one card If you feel suddenly drunk beyond your drinks, text a trusted contact your location and head to your hotel immediately; Grab is the safest exit
scams.location: Khao San Road, Rambuttri, Soi Rambuttri, tuk-tuk trips to Khao San
